title: Hiraizumi — 平泉
goal: Read a familiar water component in a new name, understand left/right, and describe a quiet visit.

blocks.text: 平泉
ひらいずみ — Hiraizumi

Hiraizumi is known for historic Buddhist sites and gardens, including Chusonji and Motsuji. It is a town in Iwate, and some of its cultural sites form part of a UNESCO World Heritage property. We will not invent a local legend or ask you to memorise dates.

**平泉に行きます。**
ひらいずみに いきます。
I go / will go to Hiraizumi.
This is the same destination structure we used across Hokkaido and Aomori. Today a simple visitor map helps us add left/right, and a quiet resting scene helps us add description and reading a book.

items: **Kanji:** 平 · **Meaning/readings:** flat; level; たいら/ひら; on ヘイ/ビョウ · **Radical and modern parts:** Indexing radical 干, かん. The horizontal/vertical and two upper strokes are useful recognition shapes · **Learning role:** Encounter. A “level surface” is a mnemonic, not a rule for all words containing 平.

**Kanji:** 泉 · **Meaning/readings:** spring; いずみ; on セン · **Radical and modern parts:** Radical 水, みず. Modern 白-shaped section above 水 · **Learning role:** Reviewed encounter. Water is the useful connection; “white water” is not the character's historical definition.

blocks.text: **平泉 / ひらいずみ**. Hokkaido gave us **温泉 / おんせん**. Here the same 泉 appears with **いずみ** rather than **せん**.
A shared kanji does not mean the two words have the same reading or refer to the same kind of site. Hiraizumi's name is not a promise that the visitor scene is a hot-spring visit.

cards.title: 左 and 右: Similar, Not Identical

blocks.text:
**左** — ひだり — left; on サ.
**右** — みぎ — right; on ウ/ユウ.

items: **Character:** 左 · **Indexing radical:** 工, たくみ · **Recognition pieces:** A shared hand-like upper-left shape plus 工
**Character:** 右 · **Indexing radical:** 口, くち · **Recognition pieces:** A similar upper-left shape plus 口

blocks.text: Focus on **工 versus 口** when the two characters feel similar. A memory aid can connect the lower pieces to the direction; it does not prove a historical reason why one direction is “work” and the other is “mouth.”
**左** and **右** often appear on maps and signs. Learn the ordinary words ひだり and みぎ before trying to memorise all their on-reading compounds.

**駅の右に店があります。**
えきの みぎに みせが あります。
There is a shop to the right of the station.

**駅の左に寺があります。**
えきの ひだりに てらが あります。
There is a temple to the left of the station.
These are **fictional map examples**, not directions to a real Hiraizumi temple. 寺 / てら = temple, an assisted character; お寺 / おてら is a common polite form.
Breakdown: 駅の右 = the station's right side; に = position; 店があります = a shop is there. Ask “right of what?” so you do not translate の carelessly or reverse the relation.

**この寺** — この てら — this temple.
**その店** — その みせ — that shop near the listener.
**あの駅** — あの えき — that station over there.
**どの寺** — どの てら — which temple?

**どの寺ですか。**
どの てらですか。
Which temple is it?

**駅の左の寺です。**
えきの ひだりの てらです。
It is the temple to the left of the station.
The second の joins **駅の左** to **寺**: the temple on the station's left. This is a connected noun phrase, not a new location verb. It extends the の pattern you already know.

cards.title: 本: A Familiar Character, a New Study Goal

blocks.text: **本** — ほん — book; also “origin/base” in other words.

You met 本 in **日本 / にほん**. Today we formally study it in a common independent word. 本 is indexed under **木**, き. Notice a 木-like structure with a small lower stroke marking the base/root area. This helps connect its “origin” meaning; the modern “book” word is learned as a word, not guessed from every stroke.

**これは本です。**
これは ほんです。
This is a book.

**本を読みます。**
ほんを よみます。
I read / will read a book.
読む / よむ is a core usable word today, while 読 stays an encounter character with reading assistance. Later communication lessons can formally study the full read/write/talk character group.

**休む** — やすむ — rest; take a break.
**休みます** — やすみます — rest / will rest.

休 uses **亻**, にんべん, a side form of 人, as its radical. The other component is **木**. A person beside a tree is a useful rest-related memory image and a clear connection between already familiar shapes.

**公園で休みます。**
こうえんで やすみます。
I rest in the park.
Compare **公園にいます** (I am in the park) with **公園で休みます** (I rest in the park). Location of existence uses に; location of the rest action uses で.
Hokkaido's reading used 休める. Today's 休む is the verb “rest.” Do not treat やすむ and やすめる as interchangeable forms of the same dictionary word.
**静か** — しずか — quiet; な-adjective, assisted kanji.

**静かな場所** — しずかな ばしょ — a quiet place.
**この場所は静かです。**
この ばしょは しずかです。
This place is quiet.
The adjective needs **な before a noun**. Compare きれいな町 and 有名な場所, building on Otaru and Noboribetsu.

For a polite negative:
**この場所は静かではありません。**
この ばしょは しずかでは ありません。
This place is not quiet.
**静かじゃありません** is also a common polite spoken negative. This description is different from **人はいません**: one says “not quiet”; the other says “no person is there.”

cards.title: A Negative Description Is Not Negative Existence

items: **What you mean:** It is not a temple · **Japanese pattern:** 寺ではありません / てらではありません
**What you mean:** There is no temple · **Japanese pattern:** 寺はありません / てらはありません
**What you mean:** It is not quiet · **Japanese pattern:** 静かではありません / しずかではありません
**What you mean:** There is no person · **Japanese pattern:** 人はいません / ひとはいません

blocks.text: The extra **では** matters. We are not saying that a temple is alive; we are identifying whether something is a temple.

For い-adjectives, reuse the other negative pattern:
**この石は大きくないです。**
この いしは おおきくないです。
This stone is not big.
Do not attach ではありません directly to the ordinary い-adjective in place of practising its own inflection.

**そして** — and then; and, adding related information.
**でも** — but, introducing contrast.

**公園で休みます。そして、本を読みます。**
こうえんで やすみます。そして、ほんを よみます。
I rest in the park. Then I read a book.

**この場所は小さいです。でも、きれいです。**
この ばしょは ちいさいです。でも、きれいです。
This place is small. But it is beautiful.
The action/place in these sentences is fictional practice. We do not promise that an actual temple allows every activity everywhere.
Keep each clause short. You do not need to turn every account into a long sentence. と joined nouns in Aomori; そして/でも connect these complete thoughts in a different way.
Our practice map places a shop right of a station and a temple left of it.

items: Which sentence identifies the temple? 駅の左に寺があります / 駅の右に寺があります.
Make **静かです** negative politely.
Which means “It is not a shop”? 店ではありません / 店はありません.
Which particle belongs in **公園＿＿休みます**? に / で.

blocks.text: **Answers:** 1 駅の左に寺があります. 2 静かではありません or 静かじゃありません. 3 店ではありません; the other says no shop is there. 4 で, because resting is an action.

items: **Location:** 平泉 — ひらいずみ; 泉 also appears in 温泉 / おんせん.
**Directions:** 左/ひだり; 右/みぎ; compare 工 and 口 to recognise the shapes.
**Positions:** 駅の左/右に…; 駅の左の寺.
**Book/rest:** 本/ほん; 読みます/よみます; 休みます/やすみます.
**な-adjective:** 静かな場所; 静かです; 静かではありません.
**Keep separate:** 寺ではありません versus 寺はありません; quietness versus a person's existence.
**Connections:** そして adds/continues; でも contrasts.
**Review:** action で; existence に; の chains; この/どの; negative い-adjectives.

blocks.text: **Lesson complete. Next location: Hanamaki / 花巻.**
